basis: Benign thymic tumor with endocrine-organ ancestry; autoimmune associations are separate diseases and do not establish immune-mediated tumor injury.
Autoimmune encephalopathy; sleep breathing dysfunction and bulbar symptoms reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than direct pulmonary injury.
Immune-mediated inflammatory engraftment syndrome with defining pulmonary deterioration/noncardiogenic edema; transient fever and rash add no axes.
Hereditary optic atrophy; intellectual disability and ataxia each occur in 2/6 patients (~33%), supporting additional neurologic involvement.
Hereditary bleeding-factor deficiency supported by abnormal bleeding; supplied evidence does not establish additional organ damage.
Oxidative phosphorylation disorder with cardiomyopathy and developmental impairment; muscle pathology in 2/3-3/3 supports myopathy. Cataract (1/3) omitted by cap.
Neuroepithelial tumor arising in the central nervous system; associated seizures involve the same axis.
Neurovisceral storage disease; hepatic failure and interstitial lung disease 80-99%; neurologic decline 30-79%. Hypersplenism (80-99%) omitted by cap.
Viral infection directly inflames the stomach.
Primordial skeletal dwarfism with severe insulin resistance and hypertriglyceridemia; hepatic steatosis in 2/2 and retinal detachment in 1/2 reported patients.
Defining congenital nasal airway stenosis and holoprosencephaly affect the upper respiratory tract and brain.
Tumor originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no additional organ involvement is established.
Congenital defect of the muscular diaphragm; associated lung hypoplasia directly impairs pulmonary development in most clinically presenting patients (>50%).
Tuberculous infection destroys vertebrae; spinal cord injury is a variable minority complication and is not required for diagnosis.
Carcinoma originates in the larynx, included in the pulmonary airway axis; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Heterotaxy with defining congenital cardiac and great-vessel malformations; organ positioning alone is not injury. Malrotation frequency is unspecified.
Melanoma originates in the eye; extraocular extension does not identify another consistently affected organ axis.
Alloimmune platelet destruction causes fetal/neonatal thrombocytopenia; intracranial hemorrhagic injury is a minority complication.
Developmental disability is defining; optic hypoplasia/atrophy 80-99% with visual impairment 6/9; hydronephrosis 30-79%. Facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
Nonsyndromic profound sensorineural hearing loss; the HGF gene name does not imply hepatic disease.
Skeletal-muscle-lineage soft-tissue tumor in the parameningeal region; proximity to meninges does not establish CNS invasion, and airway/ear sites vary.
Keratinizing lesion originates in maxillary sinus mucosa; bone erosion is possible but not established as common. This is not an ear lesion.
Benign urothelial neoplasm originates in the ureter, within the renal/urinary axis.
B-cell immunodeficiency with reduced B cells in 3/3; lymphoma (2/3) is a separately diagnosed disease. Splenomegaly alone does not establish splenic dysfunction.
Congenital endocrine hyperinsulinism; lasting intellectual/developmental impairment is occasional (5-29%). Broad nervous-system findings do not prove common lasting injury.
